TREC’s 2025 product-recommendation framework separates functional substitutes, complements, related products, and explicit compatibility grades—including “complementary but unknown compatibility.” This directly supports evidence-grounded diagnostics: extract stated device models, interfaces, dimensions, and prerequisites from titles/descriptions; preserve supporting text; distinguish explicit conflicts from missing specifications. Co-occurrence or textual similarity alone should not establish compatibility. A prerequisite absent from interaction history means “not observed,” not “not owned.” [Official task definitions](https://trec-product-search.github.io/recommendations.html)

Confidence needs calibration for the actual recommendation setting. RecSys 2024’s *Calibrating the Predictions for Top-N Recommendations* shows that good calibration across all items can conceal poor calibration among top-ranked items; it proposes rank-dependent calibration. Research on repeated implicit feedback models uncertainty in music consumption, but does not establish purchase satisfaction or equipment ownership. Thus repetition, recency, and substitute similarity can support descriptive flags such as “recent similar interaction,” while “already satisfied,” “dislikes,” and “purchase saturation” remain unknown without direct evidence. Calibration learned with sampled negatives should not be assumed valid for full-catalog recommendations. [Top-N calibration](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.11596), [Repeated-feedback uncertainty](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.02492)

Suggested adaptation: give each diagnostic supported/conflicting/unknown states; calibrate flag thresholds against available qualitative feedback and controlled examples covering explicit matches, explicit mismatches, omitted specifications, and ambiguous histories. Report precision among asserted flags, assertion coverage, and unknown rates separately by category. Selective-prediction research supports abstention when evidence is insufficient, but its guarantees require assumptions and calibration data; recommendation scores alone cannot validate compatibility or satisfaction claims. Keep these diagnostics separate from the benchmark’s macro validation HR@10. [Selective prediction and calibration](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2025/hash/3826a7e2a07ee41ca42eaf57ed337df4-Abstract-Conference.html)
